descs.t: Ukraine disputes Elon Musk's claim that its military violated Starlink's terms of service. Musk says he restricted Ukraine's use of Starlink after it was used for offensive drone strikes, while Kyiv rejects that account. We walk through what each side says and what the rules actually cover.

Elon Musk says Ukraine broke Starlink's rules by using the civilian service for drone strikes, and he limited access in response. Ukraine disputes it, pointing to the difference between Starlink and the military Starshield. We look at the claims, what Zelensky has said about drones and Starlink, and why lawmakers are paying attention.

Elon Musk restricted Starlink for Ukraine's military, said Kyiv used it for offensive drone strikes, and now says it is time for Zelensky to go. Ukraine says he has it wrong. We break down the clash, the rules at the center of it, and the bigger question: should one company be able to switch off a front line?

intro.plain: Ukraine is disputing Elon Musk's claim that its military broke Starlink's terms of service. Musk says he restricted Ukraine's use after the service was used for offensive drone strikes. Kyiv says that is not what happened. Let's go through both sides and what the rules say. Chat, who do you believe here?
intro.mid: Elon Musk and Ukraine are now in an open fight over Starlink. Musk says Ukraine used the civilian service for drone strikes and he throttled it. Ukraine disputes that, and the line between Starlink and the military version, Starshield, is the whole argument. Chat, was Musk within his rights?
intro.bold: Elon Musk cut back Starlink for Ukraine's military, accused Kyiv of using it to run drone strikes, and now says Zelensky should be replaced. Ukraine says Musk is wrong. This is about who controls the switch on a war. Chat, should any one man have that kind of power?

hook.plain: Elon Musk says Ukraine's military broke Starlink's terms of service. Ukraine disputes it. Here is what each side claims and what the rules cover.
hook.mid: Musk throttled Starlink for Ukraine, saying it was used for drone strikes. Kyiv says no. The difference between Starlink and Starshield decides this.
hook.bold: Elon Musk switched off part of Ukraine's connection and blamed Kyiv's drone strikes. Ukraine disputes it, and the stakes go far past one war.

descs.t: Ethan Klein of the H3 podcast is facing reports of an affair with a former intern, and the claims are spreading fast online. Former Try Guys creator Ned Fulmer has publicly criticised him. We walk through what has been claimed, what is confirmed and what is still only rumor.

Ethan Klein is at the center of an affair scandal involving a former H3 intern, with old podcast clips now being replayed in a new light, including one where he says he cheated on his wife. We look at what people are claiming, how the story spread, and why so many fans feel betrayed.

Ethan Klein built a career calling out other creators, and now he is facing affair claims involving a former intern who was close to his family. Clips of him and his wife on camera are going viral, and Ned Fulmer has joined the pile on. We break down the claims and what they mean for H3.

intro.plain: Ethan Klein from the H3 podcast is facing reports of an affair with a former intern, and the internet is digging through every clip. Ned Fulmer has already weighed in against him. A lot of this is still claims and rumor, so let's sort out what is known. Chat, does the H3 podcast survive this?
intro.mid: The Ethan Klein story keeps growing. Reports of an affair with a former intern, old clips where he jokes about cheating, and now other creators lining up to criticise him. I want to separate what is claimed from what is confirmed. Chat, do you think Klein comes back from this?
intro.bold: Ethan Klein spent years tearing into other creators, and now he is the one in the middle of a scandal. Affair claims involving a former intern, clips of him and his wife on camera going viral, and Ned Fulmer piling on. Chat, is this the end of H3 or will his fans forgive him?

hook.plain: Ethan Klein is facing reports of an affair with a former H3 intern. Here is what has been claimed so far, and what is still only rumor.
hook.mid: In an old clip Ethan Klein said he cheated on his wife and called it a joke. With the new affair claims, nobody is laughing now.
hook.bold: Ethan Klein built his name calling out other creators. Now affair claims involving a former intern have turned the internet on him.

descs.t: Marine Le Pen has launched her bid for the French presidency as protests sweep France. More than 400,000 people marched on Saturday over living costs and school funding, and reports say police used tear gas and made 1,300 arrests. We walk through what happened, who was on the streets, and what it means for the race.

Marine Le Pen is running for president of France at the exact moment the country is shaken by mass protests and street violence. Reports put Saturday's turnout above 400,000, with 1,300 arrests after tear gas was fired. We look at the peaceful marches, the riots that followed, the police response, and why this timing could matter for Le Pen.

France is in turmoil and Marine Le Pen has chosen this moment to launch her presidential bid. Hundreds of thousands marched, riots followed, and police made 1,300 arrests. We break down the chaos on the streets, the clashes caught on video, and whether a country this angry is ready to hand Le Pen the presidency.

intro.plain: France is in the streets. More than 400,000 people marched on Saturday over living costs and school funding, police fired tear gas, and reports say 1,300 people were arrested. And right in the middle of it, Marine Le Pen has launched her bid for president. So tell me in the chat: does this unrest help Le Pen or hurt her?
intro.mid: Marine Le Pen just announced she is running for president, and look at the timing. France has hundreds of thousands of people marching, riots after dark, and 1,300 arrests. The police are clearly done holding back. I want to go through what is actually happening on the ground and what it does to the race. Chat, is this Le Pen's moment?
intro.bold: France is boiling over. Hundreds of thousands in the streets, riots, tear gas, 1,300 arrests, and videos everywhere of police finally cracking down. And Marine Le Pen picks this exact moment to launch her run for president. This could reshape France. So chat, straight question: after scenes like these, does Le Pen win?

hook.plain: More than 400,000 people marched across France, 1,300 were arrested, and Marine Le Pen launched her presidential bid. Here is what happened and why it matters.
hook.mid: Marine Le Pen entered the presidential race just as France erupted, with 1,300 arrests after mass protests. The timing is no accident, and here is why.
hook.bold: France is burning, police are cracking down, and Marine Le Pen just made her move for the presidency. This could change France for years.

descs.t: President Trump rallied Michigan Republicans in Port Huron ahead of the midterms, joined on stage by Nicki Minaj. The rally comes as Barack Obama asks Democrats to help send Abdul El-Sayed to the Senate against Republican Mike Rogers. We walk through the rally, the speakers, and the Senate race behind it.

Trump took his midterm push to Port Huron, Michigan, with Nicki Minaj and a lineup of local speakers, while Obama campaigns for Democrat Abdul El-Sayed. Mike Rogers says he has never called El-Sayed a terrorist, and Speaker Johnson says October polls under-sample Republicans. We look at what each side is betting on in Michigan.

Michigan is now a frontline in the midterms. Trump rallied a thunderous Port Huron crowd against Abdul El-Sayed, Obama is campaigning to put El-Sayed in the Senate, and speakers on stage warned about Islamism in Michigan. We break down the fight, the claims from both sides, and why this one Senate seat matters so much.

intro.plain: Trump was in Port Huron, Michigan, rallying Republicans ahead of the midterms, and he brought Nicki Minaj with him. At the same time Obama is asking Democrats to help send Abdul El-Sayed to the Senate against Mike Rogers. Let's go through what was said on that stage. Chat, who takes the Michigan Senate seat?
intro.mid: Michigan is turning into one of the biggest fights of these midterms. Trump rallied in Port Huron with Nicki Minaj, Obama is campaigning for Abdul El-Sayed, and Mike Rogers is trying to win the seat while saying he never called El-Sayed a terrorist. Chat, does the star power actually move votes?
intro.bold: Michigan is on fire right now. Trump packed Port Huron, Nicki Minaj came on stage, and the crowd went off against Abdul El-Sayed, the man Obama wants in the Senate. Speakers warned about Islamism in their own state. This seat could decide the Senate. Chat, is Michigan going red?

hook.plain: Trump rallied Michigan Republicans in Port Huron with Nicki Minaj, as Obama campaigns for Abdul El-Sayed. Here is what this Senate race is really about.
hook.mid: Trump brought Nicki Minaj to Michigan while Obama campaigns for Abdul El-Sayed. One Senate seat, two former presidents, and a lot riding on it.
hook.bold: The Port Huron crowd erupted against Abdul El-Sayed, the candidate Obama is fighting for. Michigan could decide the Senate, and here is why.

descs.t: President Trump says he is deciding whether to make a deal with Iran or take military action, as Netanyahu warns about Iranian attacks. Trump said there would be no strikes on Iran today, a day after saying one could come maybe tomorrow. We walk through the options and what each would mean.

Trump is weighing a deal with Iran's regime against military action, says he has eyes on every entrance of Pickaxe Mountain, and calls Obama's nuclear deal the worst he has seen. Netanyahu warns of what a nuclear Iran would mean, and reports suggest Iran could be rebuilding. We look at where this is heading.

Trump says the choice is a deal or finishing off Iran's regime, and he says he is watching Pickaxe Mountain closely. Netanyahu is warning that a nuclear armed Iran would use it. We break down why another weak deal would only buy the Islamic Republic time, and what pressure could finally do.

intro.plain: Trump says he is deciding whether to make a deal with Iran or take military action. He said no strikes today, after saying yesterday one could come maybe tomorrow. Netanyahu is warning about Iranian attacks, and reports suggest Iran could be rebuilding. Chat, deal or strike, which do you think it is?
intro.mid: Big moment on Iran. Trump is openly weighing a deal against military action, says he can see every entrance at Pickaxe Mountain, and is tearing into Obama's old nuclear deal. Netanyahu is warning loudly. I want to go through what each path means for the regime. Chat, does Tehran blink?
intro.bold: Trump is telling Iran's regime it can make a deal or he will finish them off. He says he is watching every way in and out of Pickaxe Mountain, and Netanyahu is warning what a nuclear Iran would do. The pressure is real now. Chat, should Trump take any deal at all from these people?

hook.plain: Trump says he is choosing between a deal with Iran and military action. No strike today, he says. Here is what each option means.
hook.mid: Trump says he is watching every entrance at Pickaxe Mountain while he weighs a deal with Iran. Here is why the regime is under pressure.
hook.bold: Make a deal or be finished off. That is Trump's message to Iran's regime, and this time the threat comes with eyes on Pickaxe Mountain.

descs.t: Audi will build a $4.2 billion plant in Macon, Georgia, its first factory in the United States, President Trump announced with Audi's CEO on stage. The plant is set to make up to 200,000 SUVs a year. We walk through what was announced and what it means for Georgia.

Trump announced a $4.2 billion Audi plant in Macon, Georgia, right before the midterms, with Audi's CEO confirming the company's biggest SUVs will be built there. It would be Audi's first factory in the United States. We look at the promises, the timing, and what a plant this size would mean for jobs.

Audi is building a $4.2 billion plant in Macon, Georgia, its first ever in the United States, making up to 200,000 SUVs a year. For years voters were told these manufacturing jobs were gone for good. We break down the deal, why Audi chose Georgia, and what it says about where the auto industry is heading.

intro.plain: Big business news out of Georgia. President Trump announced that Audi will build a $4.2 billion plant in Macon, its first factory in the United States, with up to 200,000 SUVs a year. Audi's CEO came on stage to confirm it. Let's look at what this actually means. Chat, would you buy a car built in Georgia?
intro.mid: Trump went to Georgia right before the midterms and brought out the CEO of Audi, who confirmed a $4.2 billion plant in Macon. Audi's first American factory, up to 200,000 SUVs a year. Is this a real economic win or good campaign timing, or both? Chat, what do you think?
intro.bold: They told us factory jobs were never coming back. Now Audi is putting $4.2 billion into a plant in Macon, Georgia, its first ever in the United States, building up to 200,000 SUVs a year, with the CEO on stage next to Trump. Chat, is this the start of a manufacturing comeback?

hook.plain: Audi will build its first United States factory in Macon, Georgia, a $4.2 billion plant making up to 200,000 SUVs a year. Here is the deal.
hook.mid: Days before the midterms, Audi's CEO joined Trump on stage to announce a $4.2 billion Georgia plant. Here is what is real and what is timing.
hook.bold: Factory jobs were supposed to be gone for good. Audi just bet $4.2 billion on Macon, Georgia. Here is why that matters.
